articles.title: Indian rupee breaks six-day winning streak on state banks' dollar bids
articles.content: The Indian rupee snapped its six-session winning streak on Monday, November 9, as dollar purchases by state-run banks outweighed positive momentum. The currency touched a six-month high of 93.69 per dollar before closing slightly lower at 93.9275. Lower crude oil prices and foreign equity inflows provided some support.

articles.title: RBI's $239 bn forward dollar position to limit rupee gains despite FPI inflows: Report
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of India currently has a net short position of USD 239 billion in the forward market, which may hinder the rupee's ability to strengthen, even as foreign portfolio investor inflows improve. This influx could potentially be managed by the Reserve Bank, capping any gains for the rupee against the US dollar.

articles.title: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod to float IPO
articles.content: MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary, MMT India, has received approval from Sebi for an initial public offering. This approval follows a confidential filing of draft papers made in July. The IPO will involve the sale of equity shares by MakeMyTrip and its subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings. Proceeds from the sale are expected to enhance the cash position of the parent company.

articles.title: Indian bonds drift with oil; inflation data in focus
articles.content: Indian government bonds exhibited limited movement today as oil prices showed signs of stabilization. Investors are remaining cautious, especially with inflation data from both the United States and India on the horizon. Scheduled for later today is a bond auction totaling 290.5 billion rupees. Analysts predict yields on the 10-year bond could oscillate between 7.30% and 7.10%, with particular attention on India's October inflation report due for release this Thursday.

articles.title: Explained: Why Nvidia shares dropped 4% in overnight trade and what analysts warn can trigger a bloodbath?
articles.content: Nvidia shares dropped over 4% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice, a Chinese national, raised security concerns following intelligence reports. Nvidia has initiated an investigation into these allegations, although the board believes no secrets were compromised. Analysts suggest the company's upcoming earnings report will be crucial for market sentiment. Concerns linger over Huang's position if further evidence of wrongdoing emerges.

articles.title: Nuvama Wealth Management Q2 Results: Profit rises 19% YoY to Rs 304 crore
articles.content: Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd achieved a consolidated net profit of Rs 303.5 crore for Q2 FY27. The company saw a revenue increase of 20.35% to Rs 1,366 crore for the same quarter. Client assets reached Rs 5.5 lakh crore, reflecting a 25% year-on-year growth. Wealth management, asset services, and capital markets drove this substantial growth. The company demonstrated strong operating profits with a return on equity remaining robust at 29%.

articles.title: Nvidia falls about 3% in after-hours and perpetual futures trade
articles.content: Nvidia's shares saw a decline in after-hours trading following an announcement regarding CEO Jensen Huang. The company indicated that it is investigating potential foreign intelligence efforts aimed at Huang. Perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange and shares trading on the Blue Ocean system reflected this drop in value. The share price fell approximately 3.4% compared to Friday's Nasdaq closing price.

articles.title: Citi bullish on Indian equities, sees Nifty at 28,000 by end-2027
articles.content: Citi Research projects that India's benchmark Nifty 50 index could hit 28,000 points by the end of 2027. This forecast is based on strong earnings prospects and falling oil prices. Recent foreign portfolio investor activity has contributed significantly to the positive sentiment in the equity market. Additionally, lower oil prices could improve macroeconomic conditions and reduce inflation rates in India.

The Reserve Bank of India is anticipated to raise interest rates significantly in the coming months. Short-term bonds are expected to be more sensitive to these monetary conditions, leading to their underperformance. There are expectations for the yield curve to flatten further as short-term yields rise.
